question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.text: Berlin; Vienna; and Rome; the pact
Berlin, Vienna, and Rome; the pact
Berlin, Vienna, and Rome, the pact
Berlin, Vienna, and Rome the pact

explanation: The correct answer is B, "Berlin, Vienna, and Rome; the pact". The blank stands at the boundary between two independent clauses. The first — "In 1882 a defensive treaty quietly bound together three European capitals — Berlin, Vienna, and Rome" — can stand alone, and so can the second, "the pact committed each signatory to come to the others' aid if one of them were attacked." Two independent clauses need a period, a semicolon, or a comma plus a coordinating conjunction; only the semicolon in B fits. A comma alone (C) makes a comma splice, and no punctuation (D) makes a run-on. Option A wrongly upgrades the simple three-item list to semicolons, even though those items contain no internal commas that would require them.

_meta.anchor: The Triple Alliance (1882): Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy — Berlin, Vienna, Rome; independent-clause boundary after a three-item list

passage: Historians of European diplomacy often trace the tangle of pre-1914 alliances back to a single agreement reached in the 1880s. In 1882 a defensive treaty quietly bound together three European capitals — ______ committed each signatory to come to the others' aid if one of them were attacked.
